result.summary: This PR is a follow-up to #32587 that consolidates a previously copy-pasted `trigger_reorg()` helper (and fork construction) into `test/functional/test_framework/blocktools.py`, and converts remaining tests using `invalidateblock` to simulate reorgs into using the new fork-based helper instead. The rationale is that `invalidateblock` takes a different codepath than an actual competing-chain reorg, so tests relying on it were not exercising the intended behavior. Touched test files span wallet, p2p, rpc, and mempool functional tests.
result.problem: Several functional tests duplicated ad-hoc reorg-simulation code, and some used invalidateblock as a stand-in for a reorg despite it following a different codepath, meaning those tests were not actually validating reorg-handling behavior. This is a correctness concern for test coverage but not user-facing.

open_concerns: instagibbs raised whether an over-engineered abstraction was worth it; resolved by removing the extra ForkGenerator class and keeping only trigger_reorg

Minor pending nits: stale 'invalid' comment in p2p_sendheaders.py, wording suggestion for rpc_gettxspendingprevout.py comment, and where to add the removed cautionary comment about invalidateblock vs reorg

result.card: This PR deduplicates a copy-pasted `trigger_reorg()` helper across functional tests into `blocktools.py` and converts remaining tests that used `invalidateblock` to simulate reorgs into using a proper fork-based approach, since invalidateblock 'takes a different codepath than a reorg caused by a competing chain arriving' (description). It is a follow-up to the merged #32587 and touches wallet, p2p, rpc, and mempool test files, but only as mechanical test-infrastructure changes, not behavior changes in those areas. Review has been active: instagibbs called the added abstraction overengineered, and the author responded by removing the extra ForkGenerator class and keeping a single helper, addressing the concern. Remaining discussion is limited to comment wording and docstring placement nits. No blocking objections stand as of the latest 2026-07-30 push.
